notes_on_shape: Cleanup rules report sizes and suggest commands; the assistant NEVER deletes. Every rule states safe_to_delete per target: yes | ask_first | never.

rules.title: Free space: clean the shell's regenerable caches

fix.text: First look before deleting: measure each cache (all are regenerated on demand).
Image cache (thumbnails, notification art) — safe_to_delete: yes, regenerated by ImageCacher.
fix.warning: Regenerated on demand; expect brief re-downloads/re-renders.

fix.text: Clipboard image cache — safe_to_delete: yes (tmpfs runtime dir, volatile anyway).
fix.warning: Clears clipboard images for this session only.

rules.notes: Doc anchor is a redirect: TROUBLESHOOTING.md has no dedicated cache/state section; section 11 (Diagnostic Commands Reference) is the closest useful target (cache/log paths and cache-refresh commands).

rules.title: Free space: ccache and build logs from the installer (can reach gigabytes)

fix.text: Measure: ccache is capped at 8G by the installer; logs and failed_* files are tiny.
Trim ccache safely (keeps the tool working, drops old objects).
fix.warning: Clears the compiler cache; the next shell build recompiles from scratch (slower once).

fix.text: safe_to_delete: never — ~/.config/caelestia-kde/install.env holds your install record; keep it.

rules.notes: Doc anchor is the doc's only ccache section (stats/sizing). The installer overrides CCACHE_DIR to ~/.cache/caelestia-kde/ccache (8G cap, scripts/08-build-shell.sh), not section 1.4's default ~/.cache/ccache.

rules.title: Free space: updater repo clones (re-cloned automatically)

fix.text: safe_to_delete: yes — but the next update re-clones (slower first run).
fix.warning: Recursive force delete outside the cache scope. Updater logs live here; delete only when no update is running (see pgrep suggestion in the lock rule).

rules.title: Organize: where the shell keeps state (scheme, wallpaper pointer) — mostly keep

fix.text: State lives in ${XDG_STATE_HOME:-~/.local/state}/caelestia/: scheme.json, wallpaper/path.txt, matugen/, theme/, whatsnew.json.
safe_to_delete: ask_first — deleting scheme.json or wallpaper/path.txt reverts the desktop to the default palette on the next reseed; that is the documented reset path, not cleanup.

Your content (never delete by rule): ~/Pictures/Screenshots, ~/Videos/Recordings, ~/Pictures/Wallpapers (override with CAELESTIA_WALLPAPERS_DIR). The assistant can report sizes/counts but never touches these.

rules.notes: Doc anchor is a redirect: TROUBLESHOOTING.md has no section on the XDG state directory; section 3.4 documents the scheme/wallpaper-pointer behavior (default palette when the pointer is missing, reseed via 'caelestia scheme set -n dynamic').

rules.title: Organize wallpapers: report duplicates by name/size (report-only)

fix.text: Report same-name/same-size pairs in the wallpaper dir (respects CAELESTIA_WALLPAPERS_DIR).
fix.command: find "${CAELESTIA_WALLPAPERS_DIR:-$HOME/Pictures/Wallpapers}" -type f -printf '%s %p\n' 2>/dev/null | sort -n | awk 'NR>1 && $1==prev {print "duplicate-size: " $2 " and " prevp} {prev=$1; prevp=$2}'

fix.text: Report-only rule: the assistant will not move or delete wallpapers — dedup decisions are yours. Set the folder via Nexus -> Appearance -> Wallpaper.

rules.notes: Doc anchor is a redirect: TROUBLESHOOTING.md has no wallpaper-folder section; section 3.4's 'caelestia wallpaper -f ~/Pictures/Wallpapers/one.png' is the doc's only reference to the default wallpaper directory.

rules.title: Clean leftovers from the legacy Material You setup (documented removals)

fix.text: Check what is actually running/installed first.
Disable the legacy service (see the color-conflict rule for the full fix).
fix.warning: Disables a user service (documented migration step).

fix.text: safe_to_delete: yes — stale generated color schemes.
fix.warning: Removes generated MaterialYou color scheme files only.

rules.title: Reset the stolen-shortcuts ledger (ask first — it records your shortcut conflicts)

fix.text: Look at it before touching it.
safe_to_delete: ask_first — deleting resets the recorded shortcut conflicts; the collision index rebuilds from defaults.
fix.warning: Your recorded shortcut-theft resolutions are forgotten.

fix.text: If shortcuts misbehave after that, check the global shortcut daemon.
